Runway has shortened every month, from {{fact:e808f329-9ed2-4660-864e-85468337786f}} months at July end through {{fact:7c471ca8-9a09-435d-b265-5ad25f42b31b}} and {{fact:4e9ad01a-26dd-47bf-af8b-010049b697d1}} to {{fact:91ab4d4e-02f6-4093-9c9b-6fdd09d6ab06}} at October end. The steady decline means cash is being used faster than it is replenished. This underlying trend drives both covenant headroom signals.

Headroom on the minimum cash covenant fell from {{fact:f4a47252-f39e-4885-b92c-2417cd690951}} to {{fact:2e29a2c8-d621-4b31-a025-495dc0a2fcb6}} to {{fact:70437476-3cba-47c4-968d-bf53abaeaf98}}, with unrestricted cash at {{fact:7146bbbd-8978-474c-9d9f-b125f7f7a94d}} against a floor of {{fact:9d60030b-f402-47e5-9c64-00df9f1582df}}. This is the thinner of the two covenant cushions. The cash burn behind it also explains the falling runway.

Headroom on the minimum runway covenant narrowed from {{fact:406c40a8-c588-4040-af98-afe0429ccf53}} to {{fact:05172343-e33a-447f-929b-b97a25beb1f4}} to {{fact:d17b43e9-1b63-4865-9051-65f587a66bce}}. Runway of {{fact:d3a61e1f-0098-40b9-86a5-b0e1e3f5df58}} months still clears the {{fact:1ffb0178-4f03-45c9-945c-4f203f5e6270}}-month minimum comfortably. The signal mirrors the falling runway rather than adding a separate concern.

The breach looks real. Revenue to Plan (Section 6.3) for the three months ended October 31, 2026 came to {{fact:2aa946f7-88cb-43f5-9d81-36858ba826b6}}. The minimum is {{fact:86b794ce-e84e-4abc-994a-281808cbcc21}}, so the shortfall is {{fact:6571fa4a-90b8-4cb3-b718-3e9e95db9631}}. The borrower's own October certificate agrees: it reports {{fact:194229d5-2cee-41c8-a7b3-fc68f0dd8337}} and says the borrower was not in compliance. The test has no add-backs, so no add-back cap can explain it. Only one terms version is on file (version 1, approved, from the original agreement). No unapproved amendments are on file. A search of the documents found no waiver and no written update to the Approved Plan. Rerunning the test under version 1 gave the same failure. The September certificate also reports the borrower out of compliance with this covenant, so the shortfall is not limited to one month. How the bank responds is for the credit team to decide.

Revenue against plan stands at {{fact:d3c0308e-5362-4a2d-add5-7f48ba7438ce}}, below the covenant level of {{fact:2b1e9f12-88af-480c-8839-8321fdd53587}}, so headroom is negative at {{fact:143008c9-152b-4303-8b94-f0ec44e56200}}. The test is not merely tight but already on the wrong side of the threshold. The revenue shortfall and trend signals describe the same problem.

Revenue came in at only {{fact:7c03c73e-aea4-4930-a6c3-32d6151c4c01}} of plan, a substantial miss for a subscription business that usually plans revenue with some visibility. This shortfall is what drives the failed revenue covenant and may also explain the steady erosion in cash headroom.

Headroom on the revenue covenant has worsened each month, from {{fact:bd640ec7-ecf0-43d3-a63d-9192b211663f}} in August to {{fact:a542ff08-ffd1-4346-a466-7861b003c49b}} in September and {{fact:143008c9-152b-4303-8b94-f0ec44e56200}} in October. The miss is deepening rather than a one-off, which makes the current shortfall harder to dismiss as timing.

Unrestricted cash of {{fact:dbd79489-2b03-4727-a834-ad64cbe6d2f4}} is still well above the {{fact:470a0286-54f6-4cc7-9317-4263d93d03ed}} minimum, but headroom has slid from {{fact:fdb0de1b-4a3b-4926-a56f-074e66e78c2b}} in August to {{fact:646000c5-6cea-46af-87a0-9d19e4f548b5}} in October. Falling cash alongside a widening revenue miss may point to burn that the business is not covering with sales.

Cash headroom has dropped steadily, from {{fact:215d7fe7-96e0-4ef0-a08e-22a42452f925}} in August to {{fact:77ec4e2c-7742-43d8-8e63-8fbaa4771311}} in October. Unrestricted cash of {{fact:b9098cac-dcd5-4879-9df4-cb17ce63100f}} remains above the {{fact:a51b3150-6a6d-419b-a4d7-63750a532c0d}} floor, but the pace of decline points to ongoing cash burn. With revenue ahead of plan, the burn appears driven by spending rather than a sales shortfall.

Revenue is running at {{fact:8ea400e0-d968-48ae-b48a-e822bb1a76db}} of plan against a {{fact:7ce5a9d8-2685-45c5-b272-ba54dfb40d46}} minimum. Headroom has slipped only marginally, from {{fact:db12b9ee-916b-400d-bf72-536f72a54349}} to {{fact:901a8aea-6453-43fe-a3f4-eeb84f9282ab}}, which is essentially flat. This signal is reassuring rather than concerning, and it suggests the falling cash balance is not caused by weaker sales.
